This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.

Instrument safety checks in the generated code to catch and prevent out-of-bounds memory accesses and crashes during development. When this box is ticked the safest possible code is generated to catch and prevent out-of-bounds memory accesses during development. Invalid accesses are printed to the Nuke terminal. When this box is un-ticked then the code is generated to maximise performance without the safety rails preventing any crashes. It is recommended to enable safety rails during development and to disable once complete.

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.

description.plain_text: BlinkScript: Allows you to develop and compile your own image processing code inside Nuke to generate custom effects. BlinkScript compiles and runs a Blink "kernel" for a desired target device. A Blink kernel contains a piece of code that will run once for every pixel in an output image, and describes what computation should be executed to produce the output picture. This code is run in massively parallel processes, which makes it very fast to compute.
description.text:
BlinkScript: Allows you to develop and compile your own image processing code inside Nuke to generate custom effects.

BlinkScript compiles and runs a Blink "kernel" for a desired target device.

A Blink kernel contains a piece of code that will run once for every pixel in an output image, and describes what computation should be executed to produce the output picture. This code is run in massively parallel processes, which makes it very fast to compute.
